method: Built-in image_gen; AI-assisted reconstruction from original texture atlases.

assets.prompt:
Use case: compositing.
Asset type: complete creature cutout for a Fallout Shelter-style game UI.
Input image 1 is the EDIT TARGET: a disassembled original game texture atlas containing body pieces for this creature.
Primary request: Assemble these separate pieces into one complete Deathclaw, standing in a balanced slightly hunched bipedal pose with its horned head, torso, two arms with long claws, two legs and curved tail connected anatomically.
Preserve the supplied creature identity, original facial features, colors, flat cartoon shading, dark outlines and body-part designs as closely as possible. Reposition, rotate, scale and, where needed for paired limbs, mirror or duplicate the supplied pieces to connect them into one coherent full-body creature. Hide joints behind the adjoining parts. Change the arrangement, not the visual design; fill only small necessary connection gaps.
Composition: one creature only, entire silhouette including extremities visible, centered with modest clear margins. The creature must occupy most of the canvas and read clearly at small UI size.
Background: genuinely transparent alpha, preserving the source transparency; no scenery, ground plane, shadow or painted checkerboard.
Avoid: scattered unused pieces, texture-sheet layout, extra creatures, text, labels, watermark, redesign, photorealism, added accessories, unnecessary details.

corrections.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit target: supplied assembled cartoon Deathclaw PNG.
Fix ONLY the tail: remove the incorrect short upward-curled, rounded cat-like tail and replace it with the correct long muscular REPTILIAN Deathclaw tail. It grows from the same base at the rear of the hips, is thick at the base, sweeps low outward behind the body to the right as a heavy lizard tail, and narrows steadily to a sharp slender pointed tip. Brown leathery/scaly hide with a few small bony ridges matching the back; absolutely no fur, feline striping, tuft, rounded end or upright hook/cat curl. The full tail tip must remain inside the canvas; widen transparent margins if needed.
Keep the entire remaining creature unchanged: head, horns, face, red eyes, back ridges, muscular body, arms, claws, legs, feet, crouched pose, colors, bold outlines and flat cartoon shading.
Preserve genuinely transparent alpha background. One creature only; no ground, scenery, shadow, glow, labels or watermark.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Correct the Protectron HEAD ORIENTATION AND NECK only.

The correct head is a tall upright rounded glass-dome assembly, oriented like the Protectrons in image 3. Rebuild this from the atlas head part in image 2 by rotating that original part 90 degrees COUNTERCLOCKWISE into its proper mounted pose. Keep the dome's longer axis vertical and the curved glass occupying the tall upper/front portion; the sage-green casing forms the lower/back support. Preserve the original atlas glass panel structure and helmet contour. Use the head as shown in the official gameplay reference, not the squat broad motorcycle helmet presently in image 1.
Correct the neck joint: seat the head centered directly onto the top neck socket in the torso, with a compact short ribbed collar and the small exposed original wires tucked neatly at the base. Reduce the overly exposed raised yellow neck spring and wire gap. The head must sit naturally inside/above the shoulder line, with a clean attached joint, no floating head and no long neck.
Keep everything below the neck unchanged from image 1: torso, rounded sage-green chest panels, chest fan, both arms and hands, waist, legs and feet, standing pose, proportions, original flat cel shading and dark outlines. Single complete robot with all extremities visible and modest margins.
Preserve truly transparent alpha background, no shadow, glow, floor, extra pieces, weapons, text or watermark. Do not copy gameplay screenshot background, UI, people or a second robot.
